rationale:
The owner asked for imagery between paragraphs on built pages. The estate already HAS a section-level illustrated component (`Illustrated Text Block`: prose plus a gated <figure>, lazy loading, caption, server-resolved asset paths). Nothing chooses it. [MEASURED 2026-08-26] `component_expresses()` — the function that describes every component to the three live planner menus (build-site-planner, content-gap-planner, site-planner) — returns `[html-block, list, table]` for BOTH `Generic Text Block` and `Illustrated Text Block`. Identical. The function derives four tokens and none of them is an image, so the planner is choosing between two components it has been told are the same thing and picks the plain one: 208 live Generic instances across 23 sites versus 6 Illustrated instances on ONE site. bugs_open/381 taught the planner to see lists, tables and item sets; imagery was never added to the vocabulary. This is a missing WORD, not a missing component.

But the one-line vocabulary fix alone would have made things WORSE, and that is the second half of this submission. `Illustrated Text Block.image_url` declares source `site_assets.image`. That path is not a literal asset key: `imageryplan.imageRoleAliases` maps "image" -> "hero", and plan_sections' site_assets arm falls through to the alias because nothing ever populates r.assets["image"] (the content_data fallback fills only "hero" and "logo"). So the field resolves to THE PAGE'S OWN HERO, always — verified at the artefact, not inferred: every populated site_assets.image value in the estate is a hero asset, and 20 of 52 populated instances already duplicate an image shown elsewhere on the same page. Shipping the word alone would have taught every planner, fleet-wide, to reach for a component that repeats the hero mid-page.

So the source is repointed too, and that repoint also fixes a live latent regression: apis.uk/index has an active hero_home asset, so site_assets.image RESOLVES there, and live resolution always beats the stored-content carry — on that page's next plan_sections run all six distinct illustrations would be overwritten with hero-home.jpg. `site_assets.illustration` is not in the alias map, so it stays a literal key, resolves nothing on apis.uk, and carryStored then preserves the six good values.

Honest limit, stated because the ask is only half answered: this creates no assets. 206 active hero assets across 28 sites versus 26 illustration assets across 5, and only 4 section-scope illustration plan rows across 3 sites. Everywhere else the section renders as plain prose by design (on_missing: skip_field). The supply question is the bigger half and is NOT in this change.

plan.summary: Migration 644: add a fifth `image` arm to component_expresses (derived from the schema's declared source, not from
plan.risks:
THE COUPLING IS THE RISK, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS ONE MIGRATION AND NOT TWO. The obvious predicate is `source = 'site_assets.image'` (exact equality — it is what this lane's own plan proposed). Under the repoint the field stops carrying that value, so the narrow predicate would render Illustrated Text Block INVISIBLE again and the two halves would silently cancel, each looking correct alone. The predicate is written over `site_assets.%` for exactly that reason. Applying one half without the other is the failure mode to review for.

SECOND RISK — WIDENING VERSUS RESHUFFLE, and a row-count cannot tell them apart. 14 components gain the token. The control is not that number: it is that NO component loses a token and no component changes by anything other than gaining `image`. That distinction was established by mutation, not asserted — a variant arm that also suppressed `list` changed the SAME number of rows and was caught only by the additive assertions. Both assertions are in the migration's own DO/RAISE block and all three guards were induced and observed firing before submission.

THIRD — THE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED. Components are created by other lanes continuously (five appeared during this change's own measurement run), so a literal N is a spurious failure waiting to happen. The guards are structural and population-independent.

JUDGEMENT WORTH OBJECTING TO IF YOU DISAGREE: `site_assets.logo` is the one exclusion (site identity, 11 components, never the illustration a planner is reaching for). Every other site_assets.* image-typed field counts, HEROES INCLUDED — `hero` and `product-hero_pre_037` gain the token. I judged that a hero component genuinely does offer a server-resolved image slot, and that excluding it needs a hand-kept deny-list, which is the drift class this estate keeps filing. A reviewer may reasonably want heroes excluded.

NOT A RISK, BUT READ IT AS ONE IF ADOPTION IS ZERO: nothing re-plans a page on its own. The token reaches a model only on the next build/content-gap run, and a site with no section-scope illustration row renders the block as prose by design. Confirm the demand side before reading a zero as failure.

OUT OF SCOPE, NAMED: llm-authored alt text for a server-resolved image is a hallucination surface (a model describing an image it cannot see). It is the estate's settled convention — 13 alt fields across 9 components — and this change brings the estate's one outlier INTO it rather than overturning it. Not solved here.

edits.rationale: Half 1 — the missing word. A fifth UNION arm derived from the schema's declared `source`, matching the way html-block and items are already derived, NOT from '<img' in the template. The template route reports 47 components — every header, hero and card thumbnail, chrome the writer cannot influence; the schema route reports 14, of which 11 are menu-reachable. site_assets.logo is the single exclusion and it is stated in the file rather than left implicit.
edits.sketch:
UNION
-- 644: a server-resolved image slot the component offers as CONTENT.
-- site_assets.logo excluded: site identity, not illustration.
SELECT 'image' WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_each(COALESCE(p_input_schema->'fields', '{}'::jsonb)) f
   WHERE f.value->>'source' LIKE 'site_assets.%'
     AND f.value->>'source' <> 'site_assets.logo'
     AND f.value->>'type' IN ('url', 'image', 'image_url'))

edits.rationale: Half 2 — the source that resolves to the page hero. image_url moves to site_assets.illustration (no alias entry, so it stays a literal key and the section-scope illustration loop is what can satisfy it). image_alt moves to llm because it is typed `text` yet sourced site_assets.image, so the resolver hands it the image URL and a screen reader reads out a file path; llm is the estate's convention on 13 other alt fields and this field's own llm_guidance already assumes a model writes it.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE content_components
   SET input_schema = jsonb_set(
                        jsonb_set(input_schema,
                          '{fields,image_url,source}', '"site_assets.illustration"'),
                          '{fields,image_alt,source}',  '"llm"'),
       updated_at = NOW()
 WHERE name = 'Illustrated Text Block'
   AND input_schema->'fields'->'image_url' IS NOT NULL
   AND input_schema->'fields'->'image_alt' IS NOT NULL;

edits.rationale: The control, built into the migration rather than run beside it. A temp table captures every component's vocabulary BEFORE the function is replaced, so the guard asserts the change is purely additive against the exact population being migrated. Two assertions, because a changed-row COUNT cannot distinguish a widening from a reshuffle — proven by mutation, not assumed.

Precision and coupling guards. `unearned` fails the file if anything expresses image without a qualifying field (it fired at 372 when the arm was mutated to fire unconditionally). The Generic Text Block and Illustrated Text Block assertions are the two named halves of the coupling: the control component must be byte-identical and the target must actually gain the token, so a narrow-predicate regression that silently cancels the repoint cannot commit.

Restores the four-arm body verbatim and both original sources. Deliberately does NOT drop component_expresses() — 591/592/593 depend on it and three live planner menus call it. Carries the warning that a rollback cannot un-plan pages selected while 644 was live, and that reverting image_url to site_assets.image makes those resolve to the page hero, which is the defect 644 exists to prevent; fixing forward is preferred, with a census query to size it first.
edits.sketch:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.component_expresses(...)  -- four arms, verbatim

UPDATE content_components
   SET input_schema = jsonb_set(jsonb_set(input_schema,
         '{fields,image_url,source}', '"site_assets.image"'),
         '{fields,image_alt,source}',  '"site_assets.image"')
 WHERE name = 'Illustrated Text Block';

IF still <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '644 ROLLBACK: % still express image', still; END IF;

edits.rationale: Register entry in the SAME commit that ships the seam, per the owner ruling of 2026-07-28 condition (2). It records the alias trap (site_assets.image resolves to the page hero, always), the coupling between the two halves, the supply gap that bounds what this can achieve, and the count-cannot-see-a-reshuffle lesson — the four things a reader would otherwise have to rederive.
